meta.title: THE KING WHO SILENCED THE TRUTH
meta.subtitle: A MORAL STORY
meta.moral_line: The crown doesn't make the king... the truth does.

narration: What if everything you were told... was a lie told to your face?
This is the story of King Elio... the young king who wore a blindfold made of praise.

narration: Every morning, his advisors arrived with gifts... and honeyed words.
You are the wisest king in a hundred years, they said. And he believed every word.

narration: Only one man spoke differently. An old scribe named Dara.
My king... the granaries are empty, and the people are hungry. The hall went silent.

narration: Truth is a bitter medicine. The young king refused to swallow it.
Get out, he said. And the only honest voice in the palace... walked out into the rain.

narration: Within one season, the lies grew fat... and the kingdom grew thin.
The king looked at his charts, his gold, his empty farms. No one had warned him. No one... had dared.

narration: So the king dressed in plain clothes... and walked among his people for the first time.
And there, in a poor quarter, teaching children to read... he found the man he had banished.

narration: The king knelt before the old scribe. I was blind, he said. Then see, Dara smiled.
That day, the truth returned to the palace... and never left.
The crown doesn't make the king... the truth does.
